Broken-stick plus tail-decay inflection threshold on a numeric vector

Source: R/gap_threshold.R
dot-gap_threshold_lower.Rd

Given a vector of log-scores where low values indicate outliers (e.g. log joint probability, or -log(bridge_eta)), identify a natural break separating an outlier tail from the bulk.

Usage

.gap_threshold_lower(log_scores, threshold = 3, search_frac = 1/7)

Arguments

log_scores

Numeric vector, typically log-probabilities or -log(score). NA values are tolerated and excluded.

threshold

Multiplier controlling the strictness of the break detection. A gap must exceed threshold times the local expectation (broken-stick) or a noise floor (inflection) to count. Default 3 is HEURISTIC – the "3-sigma rule" applied loosely to the broken-stick gap distribution. Plausible range 2–5; lower values are more sensitive (more candidate breaks accepted), higher values are more conservative.

search_frac

Fraction of the sorted values from the lower tail to consider as candidate break locations. Default 1/7 is HEURISTIC: search roughly the lowest seventh (~14\ values for the outlier-tail break. (This was described as "the lowest sextile" until 2026-08-17; a sextile is 1/6 ~ 16.7\ name did not match the value. The value is unchanged.) Plausible range: 1/10 to 1/5. Note the value is effectively quantised: the implementation uses round(1 / search_frac) as an integer denominator, so only 1/k for integer k is reachable and e.g. 0.15 and 1/7 are the same input.

Value

A list with:

is_outlier

Logical vector of the same length as log_scores, TRUE for values below the break.

break_value

Numeric. Values strictly less than this are outliers. NA if no break found.

method

Character: "inflection", "broken_stick", "none", or "insufficient".

percentile

Numeric vector of empirical percentiles (0–100) for all input values, for diagnostic purposes.
